Source B is the only one that provides these correct, specific citations.

gpt.rationale: For nonpayment of rent, New Hampshire law requires the landlord to give the residential tenant a 7-day notice to quit. The eviction action may proceed only after that statutory notice period has been given.

gemini.rationale: For residential tenancies, the statute specifies that a 7-day written Notice to Quit is sufficient when the reason for eviction is the neglect or refusal to pay rent due and in arrears. This notice must be given after a demand for rent has been made.

federal.name: CARES Act §4024
federal.applies_when: Covered dwelling: federally backed mortgage loan (Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac) or covered housing program (HUD assistance, Section 8, LIHTC, rural housing, etc.)
federal.effect: During active moratorium periods: 30-day notice required before filing; no fees or penalties for nonpayment during moratorium. Emergency moratorium provisions expired July 2021 but covered-dwelling definition and notice requirements may persist under other federal programs — verify current applicability.

elements: Landlord knew or had notice of the defect
Defect substantially impairs habitability (health, safety, or welfare)
Tenant gave landlord reasonable time to repair
Landlord failed to repair
Tenant did not cause or waive the defect
substantive_defenses.note: Habitability warranty statute: RSA 48-A:14 (housing standards); RSA 540-A:2. Elements, available remedies (rent withholding, repair-and-deduct, rent escrow), and applicability as a defense to eviction vary significantly by state — attorney verification required. Statute identified via machine-assisted retrieval — attorney verification required before use

elements: Tenant engaged in protected activity (habitability complaint, union organizing, exercising legal rights)
Landlord knew of the protected activity
Adverse action (eviction, rent increase, service reduction) followed protected activity
Causal connection between protected activity and adverse action
Action was within state-defined presumption period (varies: 60 days to 12 months)
substantive_defenses.note: Anti-retaliation statute: RSA 540:13-a. Presumption period, protected activities, and available remedies vary by state — attorney verification required. Statute identified via machine-assisted retrieval — attorney verification required before use

elements: Tenant is member of a protected class (race, color, national origin, sex, disability, familial status, religion — per federal FHA; state law may add classes)
Landlord took adverse housing action
Similarly situated non-protected tenants were treated more favorably, OR discriminatory intent can be shown, OR facially neutral policy has disparate impact
substantive_defenses.note: Federal FHA prohibits discrimination in housing based on protected class. State law may provide additional protected classes and remedies. Discriminatory intent or disparate impact analysis is fact-intensive — specialist review required. grounding_gap: state fair housing case law and protected class details.

elements: Tenant had a valid lease or tenancy
Landlord substantially interfered with tenant's right to peaceful possession
Interference was intentional or negligent
Tenant suffered damages
substantive_defenses.note: Breach of covenant of quiet enjoyment — primarily common law doctrine in most states; some states codify at RLTA. grounding_gap: whether state recognizes as affirmative defense to eviction, constructive eviction standard, and remedies vary — specialist review required.

elements: Amount demanded in notice exceeds lawfully owed rent
Impermissible charges included (late fees, utilities, damages, other non-rent items)
substantive_defenses.note: Improper rent calculation — relevant where landlord has included improper charges (late fees, fees not authorized by lease) in the rent demand. grounding_gap: state-specific rules on what may be included in rent demand, and whether overcharge voids notice — specialist review required.

elements: Landlord lacks just cause ground enumerated in applicable just cause statute
Notice does not state required just cause ground
Stated ground is not one of the enumerated grounds
substantive_defenses.statute: RSA 540:2 (grounds for eviction — functional just cause requirement)
substantive_defenses.note: New Hampshire requires landlord to have a statutory ground for eviction; RSA 540:2 enumerates grounds (nonpayment, breach, nuisance, refusal to vacate after proper notice, end of tenancy). grounding_gap: "refusal to vacate after notice" ground — attorney review of current doctrine required.
